reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading is accurate (RPC path does not update observed_column_sidecars at data_availability_checker.rs:240-267, while gossip path does at data_column_verification.rs:521), but the vulnerability is cryptographically impossible. The attack scenario claims a proposer can serve 'conflicting column C2 (same index, different data, same signature)' but this violates the cryptographic binding chain: the signature covers the block header (signed_block_header), which commits to body_root, which via inclusion_proof commits to kzg_commitments, which via KZG proofs binds to the column data. If column data differs, either (1) the KZG proof fails (RPC path validates at L247-249: KzgVerifiedDataColumn::from_batch_with_scoring), or (2) the block_root differs (tracked by observed_slashable at beacon_chain.rs:3731-3737). The observed_column_sidecars cache exists for gossip deduplication efficiency, not anti-equivocation security. 01e property (01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json L299-314) states 'Anti-equivocation cache must be updated for all imported data columns' but misunderstands the architecture: observed_slashable (block-level) + cryptographic binding (KZG) provide equivocation protection, not observed_column_sidecars (gossip-level deduplication). Severity calibration N/A (dispute negates impact).
reviewed_items.spec_reference: 01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json L299-314: 'Anti-equivocation cache must be updated for all imported data columns regardless of publishing.' Property assumes cache-based anti-equivocation, but design uses cryptographic binding.
